description:
Raoping Se Zhong is an oolong from Raoping County in eastern Guangdong. It turns up on standard lists of Guangdong oolongs alongside Fenghuang Dancong and Lingtou Dancong, but little is documented about it beyond the name.

The term se zhong is the useful clue. In Anxi, Fujian, it is a collective word for the many tea varieties other than Tieguanyin. Here it probably points in the same direction, a tea made from assorted local varieties, but no firm definition is available for Raoping.

The county's famous tea is Lingtou Dancong, and the two should not be confused. Expect only what is typical of Guangdong oolong: natural floral and fruity sweetness in an orange-yellow cup.

If you find it on sale, ask which varieties went into it. Short, hot steeps are a safe start.
history: Little is documented about when or how this tea took shape. It is recorded as a named oolong of Guangdong in general lists of the province's teas, without a date or a named maker.
